name: Japanese Covered Bridge
kicker: Covered wooden bridge at the west end
summary: The roofed wooden bridge at the west end of the old town, about 18 metres long, with a small temple on the span, dogs at one end and monkeys at the other. It is the picture most visitors come to Hoi An for. Give it about 20 minutes, early in the morning before the groups or in the evening.
fee: 20,000 VND from 10 Aug 2026, or a combination ticket
heroCaption: The covered bridge from the street, roof on, water in front

notice.title: Confirm the ticket before you pay
notice.body: The bridge is one of two landmark choices on the old-town combination tickets, and from 10 August 2026 the city also charges per building. Ask at the booth which ticket covers the interior that day.

body: See the roof from the street, then walk the short wooden passage. Dogs stand at one end and monkeys at the other, with yin-yang tiles overhead and a small temple on the span. The bridge is about 18 metres long, so about 20 minutes is the visit.

Japanese merchants are credited with building it in the early 17th century. The temple was added in 1653, and Lord Nguyễn Phúc Chu named it Lai Viễn Kiều in 1719. Other official texts date the bridge to 1593 or to the 18th century.
Come in the morning, before the groups, or in the evening inside the pedestrian hours. In a flood week the river streets can be under water.

figures.caption: The temple altar inside the bridge
figures.alt: Carved wooden altar inside the Japanese Covered Bridge in Hoi An, with an incense burner and offerings

gettingThere: The bridge is at the join of Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai and Trần Phú, at the west end of the old town. Walk if you sleep in the lanes off the core. From An Bang, take a bicycle or a ride.

legs.heading: From the old town
legs.body: Walk to the west end, where Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai meets Trần Phú.

legs.heading: From An Bang
legs.body: A ride or a bicycle into the old town, then walk.

admissionNote: No separate price for this building. From 10 Aug 2026: 20,000 VND per person per building, the same for every visitor (Da Nang Resolution 98/2026). Heritage centre notices of 26 Jan and 16 Mar 2026: 80,000 VND (streetscape, Chùa Cầu or Miếu Quan Công, and two other works) or 120,000 VND (adds a museum and three other works), usable through a stay of up to three days. A May 2026 article counts those as four and six works. Ask at the booth which ticket is on sale. Free under the January 2026 notice: Vietnamese disabled people with the certificate, Vietnamese people covered by the 2003 cultural-access decision, children under 16 and pupils, Vietnamese citizens 60 and over, and diplomatic guests. Whether Resolution 98 keeps that list: Check on arrival.
